# HTextarea

> A labeled multiline field with native constraints and form reset support.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HTextarea` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-textarea>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthTextareaElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HTextarea.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Enter inserts a newline. The form adapter does not turn textarea Enter into form submission.
- The model and submitted value are strings. Choose vertical, none, or both for resize.

## Public API

label, name, modelValue, value, placeholder, hint, error: string · rows, minlength, maxlength: number · required, disabled, readonly: boolean · resize: vertical | none | both

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    modelValue?: string;
    value?: string;
    label: string;
    name?: string;
    placeholder?: string;
    hint?: string;
    error?: string;
    rows?: number;
    required?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
    readonly?: boolean;
    minlength?: number;
    maxlength?: number;
    resize?: "vertical" | "none" | "both";
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ value: "", rows: 4, resize: "vertical" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(value), change(value)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: string
    ];
    change: [
        value: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, control, hint

Use `hearth-textarea::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HTextarea } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const description = ref('A home for our apps.');
</script>

<template>
  <HTextarea v-model="description" label="Description" name="description" :rows="4" :maxlength="400" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-textarea');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Description",
  "name": "description",
  "value": "A home for our apps.",
  "rows": 4,
  "maxlength": 400
});
element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});
mount.append(element);
```
